subject.title: Feature: Include trusted sender_name in inbound metadata envelope

question: Should the trusted inbound envelope expose a human-readable sender display name, or only expose canonical principals derived from stable channel IDs, `session.identityLinks`, or operator-attested provenance?
rationale: Current main deliberately treats human names as untrusted prompt context, while the open candidate PRs propose different authority models for the same identity gap.

options.title: Prefer canonical principal
options.body: Expose only a stable sender principal when derived from stable channel IDs, identity links, or operator attestation, while keeping display names untrusted.

options.title: Allow trusted display name
options.body: Permit a trusted display-name field only after channel-specific directory authority, privacy behavior, and spoofing tests are defined.

options.title: Defer envelope change
options.body: Keep the current registry workaround until maintainers choose the trusted identity authority and candidate PR direction.

recommendation.title: Prefer canonical principal
recommendation.body: Expose only a stable sender principal when derived from stable channel IDs, identity links, or operator attestation, while keeping display names untrusted.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice spans gateway protocol, provenance, prompt trust boundaries, and channel identity semantics where this history shows substantial recent involvement.
